(14 September 2013){{cite web|title=Western Stima - Muhoroni Youth (14/09-2013 kl. 15:00)|url=http://www.futaa.com//football/event/1396176|publisher=Futaa.com|date=14 September 2013|accessdate=15 September 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130930035710/http://www.futaa.com/football/event/1396176|archive-date=30 September 2013|url-status=dead}} |matches=240 |total goals=432 |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |prevseason=[[2012 Kenyan Premier League|2012]] |nextseason=[[2014 Kenyan Premier League|2014]] |extra information='''Note:''' [[Walkover]]s counted in matches played but not counted in goals scored. |updated=9 November 2013 }} The '''2013 Kenyan Premier League''' (known as the [[Tusker (African beer)|Tusker]] Premier League for sponsorship reasons) was the tenth season of the [[Kenyan Premier League]] since it began in 2003, marking a [[decade]] of its existence. It was also the [[Golden Jubilee]] season of top division [[football in Kenya]] since 1963. It began on 24 February 2013 and ended on 9 November 2013. League champions [[Gor Mahia F.C.|Gor Mahia]] earned a place in the preliminary round of the [[2014 CAF Champions League]] while [[2013 FKF President's Cup]] champions [[A.F.C. Leopards]] earned a place in the preliminary round of the [[2014 CAF Confederation Cup]]. A total of 16 teams competed for the league, with fourteen returning from the [[2012 Kenyan Premier League|2012 season]] and one team from each of the two zones of [[FKF Division One]]. This was the first ever season for [[Kakamega Homeboyz F.C.|Kakamega Homeboyz]] in the top flight. After beating Kakamega Homeboyz on 27 October, [[Gor Mahia F.C.|Gor Mahia]] won the Kenyan Premier League title for a joint record 13th time, matching the record set by their rivals [[A.F.C. Leopards]] in [[1998 Kenyan Premier League|1998]].
